prompt: Ana says that 2x² and (2x)² are equal for every value of x. Is she correct? Evaluate both expressions when x = 3, then explain how you know whether Ana is correct.
Leo says that 3x² and (3x)² are equal for every value of x. Is he correct? Evaluate both expressions when x = 2, then explain how you know whether Leo is correct.
Nia says that 4x² and (4x)² are equal for every value of x. Is she correct? Evaluate both expressions when x = 5, then explain how you know whether Nia is correct.
solution: 2x² squares only x: 2(3)² = 2(9) = 18; (2x)² squares the whole product: (2 × 3)² = 6² = 36 → 18 ≠ 36, so the expressions are not equal; in 2x² the exponent applies only to x, but in (2x)² the parentheses make it apply to 2x

3x² squares only x: 3(2)² = 3(4) = 12; (3x)² squares the whole product: (3 × 2)² = 6² = 36 → 12 ≠ 36, so the expressions are not equal; in 3x² the exponent applies only to x, but in (3x)² the parentheses make it apply to 3x

4x² squares only x: 4(5)² = 4(25) = 100; (4x)² squares the whole product: (4 × 5)² = 20² = 400 → 100 ≠ 400, so the expressions are not equal; in 4x² the exponent applies only to x, but in (4x)² the parentheses make it apply to 4x
